14.0× Faster than Next.js SSR

While Next.js serializes JSON props and constructs dynamic Virtual DOM trees on Node.js, Yav streams compiled byte buffers directly from Rust thread memory with zero serialization penalty.

17.5× Less Memory RSS

Node.js and V8 garbage collectors hold hundreds of megabytes of object trees under load. Yav's native RAII memory management drops memory instantly the moment a socket closes.

97.3% of Raw Actix-Web

You get full file routing, layouts, typed component props, and cryptographic HMAC sessions with less than a 2.7% performance delta compared to hand-rolled raw Actix-web code.

4.4CPU Execution Profile & Time Budgetperf / cargo flamegraph

81.4% of CPU time is pure socket I/O.

Because templates compile directly into byte buffer append instructions at build time, there is virtually zero CPU cycles wasted on template parsing, reflection, or GC pauses. The CPU spends almost its entire budget doing useful network I/O.

4.5Reproducibility & Test Harnessdon't trust, verify

Execute the benchmarks yourself in under 2 minutes.

All benchmarks are 100% reproducible on any standard Linux or macOS server using open-source tools (wrk, k6). Follow the commands below to compile and execute the test harness.

bash — wrk 4.2.0 benchmark reproduction harness
# 1. Tune Linux kernel socket queue limits for high concurrency
$ sudo sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=65535
$ ulimit -n 1000000
# 2. Build the optimized release binary with Link-Time Optimization (LTO)
$ RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" cargo build --release
# 3. Run the application binary in release mode
$ ./target/release/website &
# 4. Launch wrk HTTP benchmark harness: 8 worker threads, 200 conns, 30s
$ wrk -t8 -c200 -d30s --latency http://127.0.0.1:3000/
# 5. Expected verified wrk output (preserved whitespace):
